newsitem.title: USA: Calif. home sales surge 12.5 pct in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Calif. home sales surge 12.5 pct in first quarter.

text.p: Home sales in California, the largest housing market in the U.S., rose 12.5 percent in the first quarter, according to a report Wednesday.
Between January and March of this year, more than 83,000 single family home and condominium sales closed escrow compared to 74,000 in the same period a year ago, the Experian real estate report said.

Home sales have been particularly strong in the San Francisco Bay area, while sales in the Central Valley, as well as Sacramento, Riverside and San Bernardino have been lackluster, according to the report.

"While these most recent figures suggest a healthier volume of home sales in California compared to the last couple of years, it still falls short of the level achieved in 1994 when the state experienced a brief housing market recovery," Nima Nattagh, Experians' market analyst, said in a statement.
Despite the increase in demand, home values continued to show signs of weakness in the first quarter, the report said.
In Los Angeles County, home values declined by 1.8 percent, while in Orange County, values dropped by 3 percent.

In Santa Clara County, home sales and values were up by 32 percent and 10 percent, respectively. In contrast, homeowners continued to incur equity losses in Sacramento, Fresno, Riverside and San Bernardino counties, the report said.
"Home values continue to show signs of weakness in most parts of the state, however, the rate of decline has slowed down giving rise to the prospect of a more stable market in 1998," Nattagh said.
